title: Mastering the voice system
objectives: Choose correctly between i- and -an verbs (ibigay vs bigyan, isulat vs sulatan) depending on whether the thing or the recipient is in focus
Recognize verbs whose core meaning changes with the affix (bumili vs magbili, umabot vs mag-abot)
Select the voice of each sentence so that a paragraph keeps a consistent topic and flows naturally
Read a feature-style passage and identify why the writer chose each verb form

grammar.title: i- versus -an: the thing or the receiver?
grammar.explanation:
You already know all four voices; B2 is about choosing between them when two are grammatical. The classic pair is ibigay and bigyan, both from bigay 'give'. With ibigay, the thing given is the ang-phrase: Ibinigay ko ang susi sa guwardiya — 'I gave THE KEY to the guard.' With bigyan, the receiver is the ang-phrase: Binigyan ko ng susi ang guwardiya — 'I gave the guard a key.'

Notice what happens to the other participant: whichever noun loses focus gets demoted. The thing becomes a ng-phrase (ng susi), the receiver becomes a sa-phrase (sa guwardiya). English makes the same choice with word order ('give the key to the guard' vs 'give the guard a key'); Tagalog makes it with the affix.

The same logic runs through many verbs: isulat ang pangalan (write the name down) vs sulatan ang kaibigan (write TO the friend); ibalita ang resulta (report the result) vs balitaan ako (keep me posted); ipakita ang ID (show the ID) vs pakitaan siya ng respeto (show him respect). A common learner mistake is using i- when the receiver is the point: say Bigyan mo ako ng tubig, never Ibigay mo ako ng tubig — that would mean you are handing ME over.

grammar.title: When the affix changes the meaning, not just the focus
grammar.explanation:
Some roots produce genuinely different verbs under different affixes — not just a change of focus but a change of dictionary meaning. The most famous pair: bumili 'to buy' but magbili 'to sell'. Likewise umutang 'to borrow money' but magpautang 'to lend money'; umabot 'to reach (arrive at, extend to)' but mag-abot 'to hand something over'; matuto 'to learn' but magturo 'to teach'.

The -an suffix can also create a new meaning rather than a plain locative: tawanan is 'to laugh AT someone' (tinawanan nila ako — 'they laughed at me'), samahan is 'to accompany', bantayan 'to guard, keep watch over', tulungan 'to help (someone)'. Compare sumama 'to come along', isama 'to take someone along', samahan 'to keep someone company' — one root, three related but distinct verbs.

Treat these as separate vocabulary items. When you meet a new root, never assume you can predict every affixed meaning; check, because Tagalog dictionaries list bumili and magbili as different words for good reason.

grammar.title: Voice as a paragraph-building tool
grammar.explanation:
In connected prose, voice choice is rarely random: writers keep the paragraph's topic in the ang-slot so the reader tracks one referent across sentences. Suppose a paragraph is about a package. Good Tagalog keeps the package in focus: Dumating ang padala noong Lunes. Binuksan ito ng aking ina. Ibinigay niya sa akin ang laman nito. Every sentence uses object or theme focus so 'the package / its contents' stays the grammatical star; the people appear as ng-phrases.

If instead the paragraph is about your mother, you flip the voices: Natanggap ng aking ina ang padala... no — rather: Si Inay ang nakatanggap ng padala. Binuksan niya ito at binigyan niya ako ng laman nito. Now the mother is the through-line.

When you write at B2, decide first what each paragraph is about, then let that decision pick your affixes. Random switching between actor and object focus is the single clearest marker of translated, non-native prose. A rule of thumb: new participants enter as ang-phrases with actor focus or with an existential (may/mayroon), then established participants stay in focus with object/locative/benefactive verbs.

vocab.note: ibinigay, ibinibigay, ibibigay; thing given is in focus

example.en: I already gave the receipt to the cashier.

vocab.note: binigyan, binibigyan, bibigyan; recipient is in focus

example.tl: Bigyan mo ako ng limang minuto.
example.en: Give me five minutes.

example.tl: Isulat mo ang iyong buong pangalan sa itaas.
example.en: Write your full name at the top.

example.tl: Sinulatan niya ang kanyang lola tuwing Pasko.
example.en: He wrote to his grandmother every Christmas.

example.tl: Ipakita mo sa akin ang bagong disenyo.
example.en: Show me the new design.

example.tl: Ibinalita niya agad ang resulta ng eksamen.
example.en: She immediately relayed the exam result.

example.tl: Balitaan mo ako kapag nakauwi ka na.
example.en: Update me once you get home.

example.tl: Iniabot ng waiter ang menu sa amin.
example.en: The waiter handed us the menu.

vocab.en: to hand (someone) something; to catch someone in the act

example.tl: Inabutan ko siya ng pera para sa pamasahe.
example.en: I handed him money for the fare.

example.tl: Bumili kami ng isda sa palengke.

example.tl: Ayaw na niyang magpautang sa mga kapitbahay.

example.tl: Sasamahan kita sa ospital bukas.

example.tl: Isinama nila ang bunso sa biyahe.

dialogue.title: Ang padalang naligaw
dialogue.context: Marco calls the courier's branch office about a package that was delivered to the wrong recipient.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Magandang hapon po. May ipapadala sana akong reklamo — 'yung padala ko po, naibigay yata sa maling tao.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I'd like to file a complaint — my package was apparently given to the wrong person.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.tl: Pasensya na po. Sino po ang nakalagay na tagatanggap sa waybill?
lines.en: Our apologies. Who is listed as the recipient on the waybill?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Ang kapatid ko po, si Liza Ramos. Pero ang binigyan ng rider ay ang kapitbahay namin.
lines.en: My sister, Liza Ramos. But the one the rider handed it to was our neighbor.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.tl: Ibinigay po ba niya ang buong kahon, o inabutan lang niya ito ng resibo?
lines.en: Did he hand over the whole box, or did he just hand her a receipt?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Ang buong kahon po. Mabuti na lang, kusang ibinalik ng kapitbahay kagabi.
lines.en: The whole box. Luckily, the neighbor returned it of her own accord last night.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.tl: Salamat po sa pag-unawa. Buo pa po ba ang laman?
lines.en: Thank you for understanding. Are the contents still intact?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Buo naman po. Pero gusto ko pa ring isulat ang nangyari, para may patunay.
lines.en: They're intact. But I'd still like to write down what happened, so there's a record.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.tl: Tama po iyan. Isulat ninyo ang detalye sa form na ito, tapos susulatan namin kayo ng opisyal na sagot sa loob ng tatlong araw.
lines.en: That's right. Write the details on this form, then we'll write you an official reply within three days.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Sige po. Balitaan ninyo ako kapag may resulta na ng imbestigasyon.
lines.en: Alright. Keep me posted once the investigation has a result.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.tl: Oho. At babantayan po namin ang susunod ninyong mga padala nang mas maingat.
lines.en: Yes. And we'll watch over your future deliveries more carefully.

reading.title: Ang sulat na umabot pagkatapos ng dalawampung taon
reading.tl:
Noong 2005, isinulat ni Teresita Villanueva ang isang maikling liham para sa kanyang anak na si Danilo, na noon ay nagtatrabaho na sa Saudi Arabia. Inilagay niya ito sa isang kahon ng pasalubong — mga pinatuyong mangga at isang lumang larawan ng pamilya — at ipinadala sa pamamagitan ng isang maliit na kompanya ng padala sa kanilang bayan.

Hindi umabot ang kahon. Nagsara ang kompanya makalipas ang ilang buwan, at ang daan-daang padala nito ay naiwan sa isang bodega sa Batangas. Doon natulog ang liham ni Teresita nang halos dalawang dekada.

Noong nakaraang buwan, binili ng isang negosyante ang lumang bodega. Nang buksan ng mga trabahador ang mga kahon, nakita nila ang mga pangalan at address ng mga tagatanggap. Sa halip na itapon ang lahat, nagpasya ang bagong may-ari na hanapin ang mga pamilya. Isa-isa niyang binalikan ang mga address; ang iba ay wala na, pero ang ilan ay nandoon pa rin.

Noong ikalabing-anim ng Hulyo, inabutan ng isang mensahero si Danilo — limampu't tatlong taong gulang na ngayon at nakabalik na sa Pilipinas — ng isang dilaw na sobre. Binasa niya ang liham ng kanyang yumaong ina sa harap ng kanyang sariling mga anak. "Parang binigyan ako ng huling yakap," sabi niya. "Dalawampung taon man ang hinintay, umabot pa rin."
reading.en:
In 2005, Teresita Villanueva wrote a short letter for her son Danilo, who was then already working in Saudi Arabia. She placed it in a box of pasalubong — dried mangoes and an old family photograph — and sent it through a small delivery company in their town.

The box never arrived. The company closed a few months later, and its hundreds of packages were left in a warehouse in Batangas. There Teresita's letter slept for almost two decades.

Last month, a businessman bought the old warehouse. When the workers opened the boxes, they saw the names and addresses of the recipients. Instead of throwing everything away, the new owner decided to look for the families. One by one he went back to the addresses; some were gone, but a few were still there.

On the sixteenth of July, a messenger handed Danilo — now fifty-three years old and back in the Philippines — a yellow envelope. He read his late mother's letter in front of his own children. "It felt like being given one last embrace," he said. "Even if it took twenty years of waiting, it still arrived."

gloss.en: after (a period of time) had passed
deceased, late (respectful term for someone who has died)

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'Give me the key' (the key already known, the point is handing it over)?
choices: Bigyan mo ako ng susi.
Ibigay mo sa akin ang susi.
Ibigay mo ako ng susi.
Susi mo akong ibigay.
exercises.explain: With a specific, known thing being transferred, use i- and put the thing in the ang-slot: Ibigay mo sa akin ang susi. Bigyan mo ako ng susi means 'give me a key (some key)' — recipient in focus. Choice 3 is the classic error: it literally offers YOU to someone.

exercises.prompt: Sinulatan ni Ana ang alkalde. What did Ana do?
choices: She wrote the mayor's name down.
She wrote a letter to the mayor.
She signed for the mayor.
She wrote about the mayor in the news.
exercises.explain: -an on sulat focuses the person written TO. Writing the name down would be isinulat ang pangalan ng alkalde.

exercises.prompt: Huwag mo siyang ___ — hindi naman nakakatawa ang pagkakamali niya. (laugh at)
exercises.explain: Tawanan means 'to laugh AT someone'; the person laughed at is in focus (siya). Plain tumawa is just 'to laugh'.

exercises.prompt: Nagbili sila ng lupa noong 2019. What happened in 2019?
choices: They bought land.
They sold land.
They rented land.
They inherited land.
exercises.explain: Magbili means 'to sell' — the affix flips the direction of the transaction. 'They bought land' would be bumili sila ng lupa.

exercises.prompt: Pagdating mo sa Cebu, ___ mo ako, ha? Kahit text lang. (keep me updated)
exercises.explain: Balitaan mo ako = 'keep me posted / update me'; the person receiving the news is the focus, so -an is used, not ibalita.

exercises.tl: Iniabot ng nars ang gamot sa matandang pasyente, pero hindi niya ito ininom.
choices: The nurse handed the medicine to the elderly patient, but he didn't take it.
The nurse forgot to give the medicine to the elderly patient.
The elderly patient handed the medicine back to the nurse.
The nurse drank the patient's medicine by mistake.
exercises.explain: Iniabot (i- verb, completed) puts the medicine in focus: the nurse handed it over. The second clause says the patient did not drink it (hindi niya ito ininom).

exercises.prompt: I'll accompany you to the terminal tomorrow.
exercises.explain: Samahan (-an) means 'to accompany'; kita fuses 'I' acting on 'you'. Sumama would instead mean 'to come along' with the goer in focus.

exercises.prompt: A paragraph is about a lost wallet (ang pitaka). Which continuation keeps the wallet as the topic in focus?
choices: Nakita ng guwardiya ang pitaka. Ibinigay niya ito sa opisina. Binalikan ito ng may-ari kinabukasan.
Ang guwardiya ay nakakita ng pitaka. Ang guwardiya ay pumunta sa opisina. Ang may-ari ay bumalik.
Nakakita ang guwardiya ng pitaka. Pumunta siya sa opisina. Bumalik ang may-ari.
May guwardiya. May pitaka. May opisina.
exercises.explain: The first version keeps the wallet (ang pitaka / ito) in the ang-slot across all three sentences using object-focus verbs, so the reader tracks one topic. The others keep switching focus to the people, which reads as choppy, translated prose.

exercises.prompt: Kusang ibinalik ng batang lalaki ang sobrang sukli sa tindera.
exercises.answer: The boy voluntarily returned the extra change to the vendor.
accept: The boy voluntarily returned the extra change to the vendor
The boy returned the extra change to the vendor of his own accord
The boy returned the extra change to the storekeeper voluntarily
Of his own accord, the boy returned the extra change to the vendor
exercises.explain: Kusa(ng) = 'of one's own accord'; ibinalik (i-, completed) puts the change in focus; the boy is the ng-agent.

exercises.prompt: Hindi ko pa nababayaran ang tubig, kaya bukas ko na lang ___ ang kuryente. (will pay)
exercises.explain: Bayaran takes -an because the bill (kuryente) is in focus; contemplated aspect reduplicates: babayaran.

exercises.tl: Aabutan na lang kita ng pera bukas, kasi wala akong dalang cash ngayon.
choices: I'll just hand you the money tomorrow because I have no cash on me today.
I already handed you the money yesterday.
Catch me tomorrow and I'll borrow money from you.
I'll lend you my bag tomorrow since I have no cash.
exercises.explain: Aabutan kita ng pera = 'I will hand you money'; the recipient (you) is in focus. Wala akong dalang cash = 'I'm not carrying cash.'

exercises.prompt: Show the guard your ID, then he'll give you a visitor's pass.
exercises.answer: Ipakita mo sa guwardiya ang ID mo, tapos bibigyan ka niya ng visitor's pass.
accept: Ipakita mo sa guwardiya ang ID mo, tapos bibigyan ka niya ng visitor's pass
Ipakita mo ang ID mo sa guwardiya, tapos bibigyan ka niya ng visitor's pass
Ipakita mo ang iyong ID sa guwardiya, at bibigyan ka niya ng visitor's pass
exercises.explain: The ID is the specific thing shown, so i- (ipakita) with the ID in focus; in the second clause the recipient (ka) is the point, so bigyan with the pass as a ng-phrase.
